# Local Hebrew PII detection

Ask a locally-running model whether a piece of Hebrew text contains personal data. No network call, no data leaves the machine.

The hard part is not finding an ID number. It is that many Hebrew given names are ordinary words. `אורן` is a pine tree, `אריאל` is a city, `גיל` is age, `עמית` is a colleague, `עידן` is an era, `שחר` is dawn. Names also wear one-letter prefixes, so `לאייל` is "to Eyal" and `משחר` is "from Shahar". A detector must read how a word is used, not whether it could be a name.

## Use it

Every entry point takes either raw text or a path to a file holding the text.

```bash
./pii_detect.py "דיברתי היום עם ריקי אלמוזנינו. הנייד שלה 054-7712398."   # -> YES
./pii_detect.py notes/meeting.txt                                        # reads the file
echo "האורן שליד הגדר נראה יבש, כדאי לבדוק השקיה." | ./pii_detect.py       # -> NO
echo "notes/meeting.txt" | ./pii_detect.py                               # reads the file
```

```python
from pii_detect import detect_pii

detect_pii("הלקוח דוד סרוסי, 050-3391746")   # -> "YES"
detect_pii("notes/meeting.txt")               # -> reads the file
detect_pii(pathlib.Path("notes/meeting.txt")) # -> reads the file
```

A single-line argument that names a readable file is read as a file. Anything else is treated as the text itself, so a path that does not exist is inspected as literal text rather than raising.

`detect_pii` raises `ValueError` if the model answers with anything other than YES or NO. The model loads once per process and stays cached, so a loop of calls pays the load cost only on the first one.

The script carries a PEP 723 header, so `./pii_detect.py` installs its own `mlx-lm` and needs no active virtual environment. It points `HF_HOME` at the sibling `hf/` directory, so it finds the weights from any working directory.

Speed on an M2 Pro: about 9 seconds for a one-shot command, most of it model load. Inside one process, later calls take about 4 seconds each.

## Accuracy

Measured on `dataset.jsonl`, 10 Hebrew documents holding 17 real PII spans and 28 bait spans that must stay unflagged.

| Question | Score |
|---|---|
| Does this document contain PII? | **10 of 10 correct** (F1 1.00) |
| Which exact strings are PII? | F1 0.82 |

The shipped `detect_pii` answers the first question. Span extraction is measured by `eval.py` and is not part of the CLI.

Turning the model's reasoning mode on changes the trade. It then finds all 17 spans and misses nothing, but it starts flagging bait, and each call costs about 24 seconds instead of 4. For redaction work a miss is expensive and an over-flag is cheap, so reasoning-on is worth considering. `pii_detect.py` runs with reasoning off.

## Known limits

**Feed it paragraphs, not fragments.** Accuracy drops on very short input, because there is less context to resolve the ambiguity.

| Input | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `נסעתי אתמול לאריאל בשביל הכנס.` on its own | YES, wrong |

```python
from pii_detect import detect_pii

verdict = detect_pii("הלקוח דוד סרוסי, 050-3391746")
verdict                 # "YES" — a real string, so == and f-strings work
verdict.probability     # 0.9999
verdict.margin          # 10.5
verdict.confident       # True
verdict.as_dict()       # for logging or JSONL output

detect_pii("notes/meeting.txt")               # reads the file
detect_pii(pathlib.Path("notes/meeting.txt")) # reads the file
```

A single-line argument that names a readable file is read as a file. Anything else is treated as the text itself, so a path that does not exist is inspected as literal text rather than raising.

The verdict subclasses `str`, so it drops into any code expecting a plain `"YES"` or `"NO"` while carrying the confidence alongside.

## How sure is it

Every call reports how strongly the model preferred its answer, at no extra cost.

The answer comes from comparing the model's scores for the two answer tokens, not from parsing its prose. There is therefore no reply the model can produce that leaves you without a verdict, and nothing to catch or coerce. What varies is not whether you get an answer but how much it is worth, and `margin` says so.

`margin` is the logprob gap between YES and NO. Zero is a coin flip. `probability` is the winner's share over the two answers alone. `confident` is `margin >= CONFIDENT_MARGIN`, which is 4.0.

That threshold comes from the eval set, where margins fall into two clumps with nothing in between:

| Documents | Margin |
|---|---|
| 08, 09, 03 — the three hardest | 0.25, 1.125, 3.875 |
| the other seven | 8.0 to 11.375 |

The flagged documents are precisely the hard ones: the prefixed-noun trap, `הגברת שחר`, and the ID-shaped business numbers. Confidence tracks real difficulty here, which is what makes it useful for triage. Three of ten get flagged on this set. Treat 4.0 as a starting point and re-tune it on a larger sample.

Read [`../SKILL.md`](../SKILL.md) first. The parent owns file formats, large-file inspection, stable identities, generic transcript analysis, and native Pi structure.

Smart-compaction removes redundant information while keeping contentful messages intact.

## Drop the struggle and keep the resolution

Identify a sequence of failed attempts that serves one purpose. Remove the failed loop and preserve the successful resolution.

Drop external technical failures such as user interrupts, connection retries, and transport problems.

Do not remove failed experiments that changed the technical conclusion. Those failures remain part of the story.

## Remove murmurs and technical receipts

Drop isolated narration such as:

- `Good, that worked.`
- `Now I will check the file.`
- `The file was updated successfully.`
- A tool completed with no output.
- Todo state updates.

These messages can have either the user or assistant role.

Drop local user commands that only adjust the harness. Keep commands that supply semantic instructions or trigger relevant context gathering.

## Replace structured file operations with references

Keep only the operation, path, and stable tool identity for file CRUD tools.

```json
{"type":"tool-input","name":"Read","path":"/path/to/file.py","id":"read-id"}
```

becomes:

```xml
<Read path="/path/to/file.py" id="read-id"/>
```

This rule applies to `Read`, `read_many_files`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Patch`, and `Delete`.

Expand a multi-file read into one reference per path. Preserve the source block's native provenance when available.

Pure mechanical Bash setup can also reduce to a path-only reference. A Bash command that discovers decisive information or validates completion follows the skeleton rule instead.

## Replace pivotal non-file tools with semantic skeletons

Keep the decision rather than the raw payload.

```xml
<tool-skeleton name="Bash" command="pytest" purpose="Validate the fix" outcome="148 tests passed" meaning="Proved the change before release"/>
```

# Extensions

Extensions are TypeScript modules that extend pi's behavior. They can subscribe to lifecycle events, register custom tools callable by the LLM, add commands, and more.

> **Placement for /reload:** Put extensions in `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` (global) or `.pi/extensions/` (project-local) for auto-discovery. Use `pi -e ./path.ts` only for quick tests. Extensions in auto-discovered locations can be hot-reloaded with `/reload`.

**Key capabilities:**
- **Custom tools** - Register tools the LLM can call via `pi.registerTool()`
- **Event interception** - Block or modify tool calls, inject context, customize compaction
- **User interaction** - Prompt users via `ctx.ui` (select, confirm, input, notify)
- **Custom UI components** - Full TUI components with keyboard input via `ctx.ui.custom()` for complex interactions
- **Custom commands** - Register commands like `/mycommand` via `pi.registerCommand()`
- **Session persistence** - Store state that survives restarts via `pi.appendEntry()`
- **Custom rendering** - Control how tool calls/results and messages appear in TUI

**Example use cases:**
- Permission gates (confirm before `rm -rf`, `sudo`, etc.)
- Git checkpointing (stash at each turn, restore on branch)
- Path protection (block writes to `.env`, `node_modules/`)
- Custom compaction (summarize conversation your way)
- Conversation summaries (see `summarize.ts` example)
- Interactive tools (questions, wizards, custom dialogs)
- Stateful tools (todo lists, connection pools)
- External integrations (file watchers, webhooks, CI triggers)
- Games while you wait (see `snake.ts` example)

See [examples/extensions/](../examples/extensions/) for working implementations.

# Synthetic messages, turns, and delivery lifecycle

Use this model whenever an extension injects information into a Pi session. The crucial distinction is not visual presentation; it is whether the payload becomes an agent message at all.

## Choose the channel by who must know

### `pi.appendEntry()` is for the user alone

`pi.appendEntry(customType, data)` persists extension data in the session but **never adds it to LLM context**. Pair it with `pi.registerEntryRenderer()` to show durable TUI content in the transcript.

Use this when the main agent must remain permanently oblivious. This is the only transcript-visible channel with that guarantee.

- Entries survive reloads.
- Entry renderer `data` is optional in the SDK type; guard it.
- Rendering an entry does not make it a message.
- `display: false` on a custom message is not an alternative: hiding UI does not hide content from the LLM.

### `pi.sendMessage()` always creates agent-visible context

`pi.sendMessage()` creates a custom synthetic message. Its `content` participates in LLM context. `deliverAs` and `triggerTurn` control *when* the agent receives it, not *whether* the agent receives it.

Never use `sendMessage()` for information the main agent must not eventually see. In particular, `deliverAs: "nextTurn"` means “later,” not “never.”

### `pi.sendUserMessage()` impersonates a user turn

`pi.sendUserMessage()` creates an actual user-role message and always triggers agent work. When idle it starts a turn immediately. When streaming, the caller must choose `deliverAs: "steer"` or `"followUp"`.

Prefer a custom message when synthetic provenance matters. Use `sendUserMessage()` only when the extension intentionally wants the same semantics as user-authored input.

## `sendMessage()` follows a first-match-wins state machine

The runtime evaluates these branches in order:

```text
1. deliverAs === "nextTurn"
   → buffer in _pendingNextTurnMessages

2. agent is streaming
   → deliverAs === "followUp" ? follow-up queue : steering queue

3. triggerTurn === true
   → append the custom message and start an LLM turn immediately

4. otherwise
   → append and persist the custom message without starting a turn
```

This precedence is the mental model. Do not reason about `deliverAs × triggerTurn` as six equally independent combinations:

- `deliverAs` distinguishes queues while streaming.
- `triggerTurn` distinguishes behaviors while idle.
- `nextTurn` is checked first and overrides both current state and `triggerTurn`.

| `deliverAs` | `triggerTurn` | Agent idle | Agent streaming |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `"steer"` or omitted | `false` | Append silently; visible on a later turn | Queue as steering |
| `"steer"` or omitted | `true` | Start a turn immediately | Queue as steering; `triggerTurn` ignored |
| `"followUp"` | `false` | Append silently | Queue as follow-up |
| `"followUp"` | `true` | Start a turn immediately | Queue as follow-up; `triggerTurn` ignored |
| `"nextTurn"` | either | Buffer until the next user prompt | Buffer until the next user prompt |

## The overlay already has the right insertion point

`runner.ts:85` builds child sessions with `createAgentSessionServices({ cwd, agentDir, settingsManager, ... })`. `runner.ts:420` then calls `session.bindExtensions({ mode: "print" })`. Child sessions can therefore load enabled global extensions.

The overlay later renders captured history independently. `widget.ts:898` gets messages through `transcriptMessages()`:

- A running agent uses `agent.session.agent.state.messages.slice(agent.inheritedMessageCount)`.
- A finished agent uses `agent.messages`.

Rendering follows this path:

`AgentViewer.render(width)` → `contentLines(innerWidth)` → `transcriptLines(width)` → `messageLines(message, width)`

The overlay is a line-array producer, not a mounted component host. `messageLines()` returns `string[]`. It has no component registry or lifecycle, and it does not call `invalidate()`.

That structure still supports the copied renderers. The assistant-text branch already constructs Pi's `Markdown` component, calls `.render(width)`, and appends the returned lines. Any local object that implements `render(width): string[]` can use the same boundary.

The real overlay width reaches `messageLines()`. The overlay opens at 90% terminal width and 70% terminal height. `transcriptLines()` later calls `truncateToWidth(line, width)` on every line. This hard-cuts wide output rather than wrapping it. Every copied renderer must therefore use the supplied overlay width.

Do not instantiate Pi's live `ToolExecutionComponent` in the overlay. It resolves current tool definitions and models live execution state. The overlay displays historical child-session data whose current definitions may differ or no longer exist.

## Two sites create the raw appearance

`widget.ts:867` renders calls as:

```ts
`${part.name} ${JSON.stringify(part.arguments)}`
```

`widget.ts:879` renders results as a bracketed tool name followed by wrapped raw output:

```ts
`[${message.toolName}]`
```

`capTranscript()` then cuts output at `TRANSCRIPT_OUTPUT_CAP = 500` characters. This is a character cap, not a line-aware preview.

A second site uses the same raw call presentation. `describeAssistantPart()` in `widget.ts:522` builds the one-line activity preview below the editor. The implementation must fix both sites.

1. `read`
2. `edit`

## App-true gifts (must pass)

1. **Streaming + reasoning.**
   Falsify: send a prompt on a reasoning model; answer text appears only after completion, or no reasoning block with content renders.
   Done: text grows incrementally during the turn; a reasoning block renders, expands and collapses, and contains the reasoning text.

2. **Tool cards with live output.**
   Falsify: a prompt forcing `for i in 1..5; echo; sleep 1` shows no tool card, or the card's output appears only after the tool finishes.
   Done: the card shows tool name + args, its output grows while the tool runs, and the final result persists on the card.

3. **Thread list + resume.**
   Falsify: after creating two sessions with distinct content and reloading the page, a session is missing, or opening one renders incomplete history.
   Done: both sessions listed after reload; opening each renders its full transcript.

4. **Rename.**
   Falsify: a renamed thread reverts after reload, or its id changes.
   Done: the new title persists across reload on the same thread id.

5. **Stop mid-run.**
   Falsify: during `sleep 60`, Stop leaves the run running (indicator persists, output continues) or errors the app.
   Done: the run halts promptly and the UI returns to idle with the interrupted transcript intact.

6. **Model + thinking controls.**
   Falsify: an idle-thread model switch is not reflected in the next turn's metadata, or a thinking-level change never lands in the effective config.
   Done: selection and level are reflected in thread config/metadata and the next reply.

7. **Mid-run queue (default lane).**
   Falsify: sending while running throws, or the message neither appears in the queue card nor ever reaches the transcript.
   Done: the mid-run send appears in the queue card, is delivered per its lane when due, and Clear restores the text to the composer.

8. **Context usage.**
   Falsify: after a completed turn no usage indicator renders, or a cold thread (fresh server, no live session) shows none.
   Done: the ring/percent renders from live turns and from cold-thread reads.

9. **Image passthrough** (model-dependent; run on a vision-capable model).

# Extracting the web GUI into the assistant-ui fork (the cookiecutter)

## Why

Gilad forked upstream assistant-ui to turn the Avidor web GUI into a reusable cookiecutter for future Israeli clients. Desired end state: a new client wants a chat GUI → fork the fork → "sure", not "I need to figure out how to port it".

The discovery that reshaped the plan: upstream now ships **`@assistant-ui/react-pi`** (a first-class Pi adapter, plus a full `examples/with-pi` Next app). The spike's founding premise — "Pi is not a first-class assistant-ui citizen" — is obsolete. Upstream's adapter covers most of the hand-rolled bridge, absorbs `projection.mjs` (Pi pre-1.0 schema tracking), and has tests over that surface. Verifier round 1 then sharpened this: **package support ≠ working app behavior** — five signed-off gifts are package-true but app-false (list below), so CP 1 falsifies end-to-end through `apps/chat`, not through package README claims.

## Decisions (26-08-11, Gilad)

- decided:: Adopt react-pi **wholesale**; hand-rolled equivalents are thrown away at M1 CP 1. rationale:: upstream carries Pi's schema-tracking cost from now on.
- decided:: The fork IS the cookiecutter. A new client repo = a fork of the fork. First one: `avidor-assistant-ui` (M2).
- decided:: The app lives in a new fork-owned dir (working name `apps/chat`), **seeded from `examples/with-pi`**. rationale:: upstream never edits our dir, so `git merge upstream/main` stays clean; `with-pi` stays a pristine reference to diff for future gifts.
- decided:: Deploy/devops/PII stay per-client and never enter the fork. Pi is assumed — no agent-runtime abstraction.
- rule:: PII tie-breaker (standing): the fork makes no PII-ready moves. But at a genuine decision fork where path A makes later PII work very hard and path B is cheap, take B. Not expected to actually occur.

## Verifier round 1 (26-08-11) — verdict: confirmed, sets revised

Every claim was checked against upstream source (not taken on faith). All confirmed:

1. **Reconnect is not snapshot-first after initial load.** The live stream subscribes `?snapshot=false` (`ThreadController.connect` passes `includeSnapshot: loadState !== "loaded"`; `httpClient.subscribe` bakes it into the URL) and `openPiEventStream`'s reconnect loop reuses that URL forever; the reducer accepts seq gaps silently (`threadState.ts` dedups only `seq <= lastSeq`). A network blip that swallows `message_end`/`agent_end` leaves the UI streaming forever; tab reload recovers, reconnect does not.
2. **Credentials never gate sending.** `mapping.ts#deriveReadiness` knows only `missing-model`/`ready`; the handshake computes accurate `missing-credentials` and the app can banner it (observed live at CP 1), but live readiness overrides it once present and nothing gates the composer — a credential-less send fails late (`POST /threads` 500) with the message silently vanishing. `refined:: 26-08-11 15:05 by the CP 1 anchor run.`
3. **Notices exist only in adapter extras.** `compaction`/`retry`/`lastError` are exposed by `usePiRuntimeExtras`; the with-pi app renders none of them.
4. **One send affordance mid-run.** Both queue lanes (follow-up + steer) live in the package; the app exposes only the default send path and a queue card with Clear.
5. **Tool-associated `select`/`input`/`editor` dialogs dismiss instead of collecting input.** `packages/ui` `ToolFallbackApproval.respond` sends `resume({approved: boolean})`; `responseForInterrupt` finds no string value → `{dismissed: true}`. Only free-standing requests get the value-collecting card.
6. **The supervisor is host-unconfigurable where it matters.** `SessionManager.create(cwd)` with no sessions dir; `list`/`listAll` on the default store; uncurated `getAvailableModels`; unconstrained `setModel`; catalog `ModelRuntime` split from each session's own auth (a runtime-only key set on one never reaches the other); message ids positional (`pi-msg:N`); no running-session count on `PiClient` (derivable via `listThreads` status — adequacy for the idle deploy gate decided at CP 3).
7. **`with-pi` has no deployable artifact shape.** Dynamic `next start`, four `workspace:*` runtime deps, tsconfig paths that resolve `@/components/assistant-ui/*` into `packages/ui/src/` (monorepo-relative), no standalone output config.
8. **Archive/delete and the workspace browser are not acceptance-grade.** Archive state is process-local and non-durable; the workspace browser is a dev-only directory picker. Neither counts as a gift.

## Verifier round 2 (checkpoint 1, 26-08-11 15:26) — accepted in full

1. CP 1 baseline restated: **9 GREEN + anchor-10 PARTIAL**, not 10/10 — live rendering of tool-associated dialogs fails (proven confirm+select; input/editor untested on that path; root cause unproven, shared-cause-with-reconnect kept as a hypothesis).
2. The five expected-RED repairs + anchor-10 are now explicitly inventoried under **CP 2a** (they had silently stayed under .gift).
3. The seam gained criterion 10 — **server-authoritative workspace confinement** (client-supplied `workspacePath` override verified in the seeded routes).
4. Repo topology: no private fork exists inside a public fork network — M2 client repos become private standalone mirrors (M2 flag 5); generic-fork visibility flagged to Gilad.
5. Non-acceptance surfaces (workspace picker, archive, delete) got an explicit removal disposition at CP 2c.
6. Truth fixes applied: anchors-doc frontmatter/verdict, and `apps/chat/README.md`'s inherited claims (both queue lanes, working blocking dialogs) corrected in the fork.

## The four sets (M1 Prep 1 + Prep 2 output, revised)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CP 2a reproduction harness — one scenario per proven repair.
# Usage: ./scenario.sh <retry|compaction|handshake-fail|handshake-slow|noauth|stop|status>
set -euo pipefail

# shellcheck source=lib/common.sh
. "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

SCENARIO="${1:-}"

# A harness that exits silently is worse than one that fails: say so, and take
# down whatever earlier steps already started. Without this, a scenario that
# died at the app left the mock provider holding its port, so the retry hit
# "port held by someone else" and refused to run.
trap 'status=$?; [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { printf "harness: aborted (exit %s); stopping what it started\n" "$status" >&2; harness_stop; }; release_run_lock' EXIT

usage() {
  cat <<'TXT'
usage: ./scenario.sh <scenario>

  retry            mock provider rejects the first completion; the composer
                   shows the auto-retry notice during the backoff
  compaction       mock provider reports a prompt over the compaction
                   threshold; the composer shows the compaction notice
  handshake-fail   the handshake answers 500; sending is blocked with the
                   reason on screen
  handshake-slow   the handshake is held open; sending is blocked while it
                   loads, then opens
  noauth           no credentials for the selected model; sending is blocked
                   with the readiness message
  seam             the host configuration: an isolated session store that
                   survives a restart, a curated model menu that setModel
                   enforces, new-session defaults, durable message ids, a
                   confined workspace enforced by id as well as by listing,
                   the running-session count, and a resume whose saved model
                   has no credentials
  seam-seed-unready
                   the other readiness pairing: the seeded model has no
                   credentials but the open thread can run, so the composer
                   follows the thread. Run `seam` first.
  transcript       what every reader must agree on: a compaction that replaces
                   the transcript under a connected client, and a retry whose
                   failed attempt Pi drops from its own array
  admission        who owns a prompt between the POST and Pi: two prompts and a
                   Clear inside the settled hook, and one-at-a-time admission
                   through a held-open preflight
  settlement       what a settlement belongs to: two runs whose settled hooks
                   overlap, and a prompt sent while Pi still owes one

  stop             kill everything this harness started
  status           show what is running

Scenarios need no secrets and make no real model calls.
Override the fork location with AUI_FORK=/path/to/assistant-ui.
TXT
}

scenario_retry() {
  harness_reset
  reset_sessions mock

scenario_transcript() {
  harness_reset
  rm -f "$RUN_DIR"/*.log
  reset_sessions mock
  SEAM_SESSIONS="$RUN_DIR/transcript-sessions"
  rm -rf "$SEAM_SESSIONS"
  mkdir -p "$SEAM_SESSIONS"
  MOCK_PROMPT_TOKENS=400 start_mock_provider
  APP_ENV=(PI_SESSIONS_DIR="$SEAM_SESSIONS")
  start_app mock mockery mock-1

  base="http://localhost:$APP_PORT/api/pi"
  thread="$(api -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' "$base/threads" \
    | jq -r '.metadata.id')"
  api -o /dev/null -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d '{"input":{"content":"first"}}' "$base/threads/$thread/messages"
  wait_thread_idle "$base" "$thread"

  # Compaction, through a connected subscriber. Pi replaces the transcript
  # while a client is attached, and ids alone cannot repair that client.
  say ""
  say "compaction, watched by a connected client:"
  stop_service mock-provider
  wait_port_free "$MOCK_PORT"
  MOCK_PROMPT_TOKENS=5000 MOCK_LOG_SYSTEM=1 start_mock_provider

  compact_stream="$RUN_DIR/compaction.sse"
  : >"$compact_stream"
  curl -sN --max-time 60 "$base/threads/$thread/events" >"$compact_stream" 2>/dev/null &
  compact_pid=$!
  sleep 2
  api -o /dev/null -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d '{"input":{"content":"push it over the threshold"}}' \
    "$base/threads/$thread/messages"
  wait_thread_idle "$base" "$thread"
  waited=0
  while [ "$waited" -lt 20 ] && ! grep -q 'compactionSummary' "$compact_stream"; do
    sleep 1
    waited=$((waited + 1))
  done
  kill "$compact_pid" 2>/dev/null || true

  expect_contains "the replaced transcript reaches the connected client" \
    "$(grep -o 'compactionSummary' "$compact_stream" | head -1)" compactionSummary

#!/usr/bin/env bash

script_name=${0##*/}

grouped() {
    printf "%'d" "$1"
}

main() {
    if (( $# == 0 )); then
        printf 'usage: %s <path> [path ...]\n' "$script_name" >&2
        return 2
    fi

    export LC_NUMERIC=en_US.UTF-8

    local path relative_path size bytes lines words tokens sort_key absolute_path tab
    local -a rows=()
    tab=$'\t'

    for path in "$@"; do
        if [[ $path == /* ]]; then
            absolute_path=$path
        else
            absolute_path=$PWD/$path
        fi
        relative_path=${absolute_path#$PWD/}

        if [[ ! -e $path ]]; then
            rows+=("-2${tab}0${tab}0${tab}0${tab}${relative_path}${tab}Does not exist")
            continue
        fi

        if [[ -d $path ]]; then
            rows+=("-2${tab}0${tab}0${tab}0${tab}${relative_path}${tab}Directory, not a file")
            continue
        fi

        size=$(du -h "$path" | awk '{print $1}')
        bytes=$(stat -f%z "$path")
        lines=$(wc -l < "$path" | tr -d ' ')
        words=$(wc -w < "$path" | tr -d ' ')
        if LC_ALL=C grep -qI . "$path"; then
            tokens=$(ttok < "$path")
            sort_key=$tokens
            tokens=$(grouped "$tokens")
        else
            tokens='<binary>'
            sort_key=-1
        fi

        rows+=("${sort_key}${tab}${words}${tab}${lines}${tab}${bytes}${tab}${relative_path}${tab}${size}${tab}$(grouped "$lines")${tab}$(grouped "$words")${tab}${tokens}")
    done

    printf 'path\tsize\tlines\twords\ttokens\n'
    printf '%s\n' "${rows[@]}" \
        | sort -t$'\t' -k1,1nr -k2,2nr -k3,3nr -k4,4nr \
        | cut -f5-
}

 * the one `ModelRuntime` behind it. Imported only from route handlers — never

APP=/opt/avidor

verify_shipped_file() {
  local local_file="$1" remote_file="$2" expected actual
  expected="$(shasum -a 256 "$local_file" | awk '{print $1}')"
  actual="$(gcloud compute ssh "$INSTANCE" --zone="$ZONE" --quiet \
    --command="sha256sum $remote_file | awk '{print \$1}'")"
  [ "$actual" = "$expected" ] || {
    echo "FATAL: shipped checksum mismatch: $remote_file" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  echo "  $remote_file: $actual"

# --- process ownership ------------------------------------------------------
# This machine is shared, so the harness signals a process only when it can
# prove it started that process: same pid, same start time (a recycled pid will
# not match), and a process-group leader, which is what spawn-detached makes
# every service. Anything else is left alone, loudly.

process_start_time() { ps -o lstart= -p "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' '; }
process_group() { ps -o pgid= -p "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '; }
process_command() { ps -o command= -p "$1" 2>/dev/null; }

service_pid() { sed -n 1p "$RUN_DIR/$1.pid" 2>/dev/null; }

start_bg() {
  name="$1"
  shift
  pid="$(node "$HARNESS_DIR/lib/spawn-detached.mjs" "$RUN_DIR/$name.log" "$@")" ||
    die "could not start $name"
  sleep 1 # let the child exist before its start time is read
  printf '%s\n%s\n' "$pid" "$(process_start_time "$pid")" >"$RUN_DIR/$name.pid"
}

# True only for a live process this harness started and still owns.
owns_process() {
  pidfile="$RUN_DIR/$1.pid"
  [ -e "$pidfile" ] || return 1
  pid="$(sed -n 1p "$pidfile")"
  recorded_start="$(sed -n 2p "$pidfile")"
  [ -n "$pid" ] || return 1
  kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  [ "$(process_start_time "$pid")" = "$recorded_start" ] || return 1
  [ "$(process_group "$pid")" = "$pid" ] || return 1
  return 0
}

"""The unmask daemon (production shape: its own user `avidor-unmask`, the sole reader of the
identity table). Localhost-only HTTP. Every request is gated on an in-process IAP JWT check — the
one auth decision that cannot be delegated to the load balancer, because the agent shares the
bridge's OS user and can reach this port on localhost. A request the agent forges has no valid
IAP assertion and dies at verification.

The transform is a CRM_KEY join (new-plan architecture, 26-07-11): six `real_*` identity columns
are APPENDED to a CSV artifact, values joined from the identity table by each row's CRM_KEY.
Original bytes are never rewritten; anything the join cannot serve exactly passes through
untouched with a reason in `X-Unmask-Status` — exact or absent, never guessed. (The bridge
forwards `x-unmask-*` headers as-is, so the header names keep that prefix.)

Security posture:
- Binds 127.0.0.1 only (config default; never 0.0.0.0). Localhost-reachable BY DESIGN — the JWT
  is the gate, not the network.
- Auth failure → bodyless 403, no reason echoed (no oracle). The reason goes to stderr only.
- Takes the artifact bytes in the request body (the bridge reads the file, realpath-guarded, and
  forwards the bytes + the original IAP header). The daemon therefore needs NO filesystem access
  to the artifact desk — its only inputs are the JWT and the body, and its only privileged read
  is the identity table. There is no code path that reads an arbitrary file.
- Never logs request bodies or enriched output (that would write PII to the journal).

Endpoints:
  GET  /health   liveness, no auth, no data
  POST /unmask   body = artifact bytes; header x-goog-iap-jwt-assertion = IAP JWT;
                 ?name=<filename> selects CSV handling. -> enriched bytes + X-Unmask-* headers
"""

"""Read-only access to the identity table — the only PII at rest (new-plan §Components).

Opens the DuckDB file per lookup, so the nightly's atomic `os.replace` of the file needs no
daemon restart: an in-flight lookup keeps its already-open inode, the next lookup sees the new
file. Raises SystemExit at construction if the DB is missing or has the wrong shape (the daemon
must refuse to start over a broken identity source), and IdentityUnavailable at lookup time if
the file degrades mid-serve (mapped to a bodyless 503 upstream).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import duckdb

EXPECTED_COLUMNS = [
    "crm_key",
    "first_name",
    "last_name",
    "mobile_phone",
    "home_phone",
    "email",
    "national_id",
]


class IdentityUnavailable(Exception):
    """The identity DB cannot be read right now — fail closed, serve nothing."""


class IdentityReader:
    def __init__(self, path: str):
        self.path = path
        try:
            connection = duckdb.connect(path, read_only=True)
            columns = [row[0] for row in connection.execute("DESCRIBE identity").fetchall()]
            connection.close()
        except duckdb.Error as exc:
            raise SystemExit(f"FATAL: identity DB unreadable at {path}: {exc}") from exc
        if columns != EXPECTED_COLUMNS:
            raise SystemExit(f"FATAL: identity DB columns {columns} != {EXPECTED_COLUMNS}")

    def lookup(self, keys: list[int]) -> dict[int, tuple[str, ...]]:
        """CRM keys -> their six identity values ('' for NULL). Keys are validated ints, so the
        IN-list literal is injection-safe by construction."""
        unique_keys = sorted(set(keys))
        if not unique_keys:
            return {}
        in_list = ",".join(str(key) for key in unique_keys)
        try:
            connection = duckdb.connect(self.path, read_only=True)
            connection.execute("SET threads TO 1")
            rows = connection.execute(f"SELECT * FROM identity WHERE crm_key IN ({in_list})").fetchall()
            connection.close()
        except duckdb.Error as exc:
            raise IdentityUnavailable(str(exc)) from exc
        return {row[0]: tuple("" if value is None else str(value) for value in row[1:]) for row in rows}

import json
import os
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

TOKEN = re.compile(r"(?:^|\s)/([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)")
FRONTMATTER_NAME = re.compile(r"^name:\s*(.+?)\s*$", re.MULTILINE)


def find_skill(name: str, cwd: Path) -> Path | None:
    """Return the SKILL.md path for `name`, project dir preferred over user dir."""
    for base in (cwd / ".claude" / "skills", Path.home() / ".claude" / "skills"):
        candidate = base / name / "SKILL.md"
        if candidate.is_file():
            return candidate
    return None


def frontmatter_name(body: str, fallback: str) -> str:
    """Extract `name:` from the leading --- frontmatter block, else `fallback`."""
    if not body.startswith("---"):
        return fallback
    end = body.find("\n---", 3)
    if end == -1:
        return fallback
    match = FRONTMATTER_NAME.search(body[:end])
    return match.group(1).strip("\"'") if match else fallback

def _message_timestamp_datetime(timestamp: str | None) -> datetime | None:
    """
    Parse a message timestamp into local time.

    >>> _message_timestamp_datetime("2026-06-21T09:30:00").date().isoformat()
    '2026-06-21'
    >>> _message_timestamp_datetime(None) is None
    True
    """
    if timestamp is None:
        return None
    parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(timestamp.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    if parsed.tzinfo is None:
        return parsed
    return parsed.astimezone().replace(tzinfo=None)


def _ordinal_day(day: int) -> str:
    """
    Render a calendar day with an English ordinal suffix.

    >>> [_ordinal_day(day) for day in (1, 2, 3, 4, 11, 12, 13, 21)]
    ['1st', '2nd', '3rd', '4th', '11th', '12th', '13th', '21st']
    """
    if 10 <= day % 100 <= 20:
        return f"{day}th"
    suffix = {1: "st", 2: "nd", 3: "rd"}.get(day % 10, "th")
    return f"{day}{suffix}"

# --- process ownership ------------------------------------------------------
# This machine is shared, so the harness signals a process only when it can
# prove it started that process: same pid, same start time (a recycled pid will
# not match), and a process-group leader, which is what spawn-detached makes
# every service. Anything else is left alone, loudly.

process_start_time() { ps -o lstart= -p "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' '; }
process_group() { ps -o pgid= -p "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '; }
process_command() { ps -o command= -p "$1" 2>/dev/null; }

    die "could not start $name"
  sleep 1 # let the child exist before its start time is read
  printf '%s\n%s\n' "$pid" "$(process_start_time "$pid")" >"$RUN_DIR/$name.pid"
}

# True only for a live process this harness started and still owns.
owns_process() {
  pidfile="$RUN_DIR/$1.pid"
  [ -e "$pidfile" ] || return 1
  pid="$(sed -n 1p "$pidfile")"
  recorded_start="$(sed -n 2p "$pidfile")"
  [ -n "$pid" ] || return 1
  kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  [ "$(process_start_time "$pid")" = "$recorded_start" ] || return 1
  [ "$(process_group "$pid")" = "$pid" ] || return 1
  return 0
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CP 2a reproduction harness — one scenario per proven repair.
# Usage: ./scenario.sh <retry|compaction|handshake-fail|handshake-slow|noauth|stop|status>
set -euo pipefail

# shellcheck source=lib/common.sh
. "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

SCENARIO="${1:-}"

# A harness that exits silently is worse than one that fails: say so, and take
# down whatever earlier steps already started. Without this, a scenario that
# died at the app left the mock provider holding its port, so the retry hit
# "port held by someone else" and refused to run.
trap 'status=$?; [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { printf "harness: aborted (exit %s); stopping what it started\n" "$status" >&2; harness_stop; }; release_run_lock' EXIT

usage() {
  cat <<'TXT'
usage: ./scenario.sh <scenario>

  retry            mock provider rejects the first completion; the composer
                   shows the auto-retry notice during the backoff
  compaction       mock provider reports a prompt over the compaction
                   threshold; the composer shows the compaction notice
  handshake-fail   the handshake answers 500; sending is blocked with the
                   reason on screen
  handshake-slow   the handshake is held open; sending is blocked while it
                   loads, then opens
  noauth           no credentials for the selected model; sending is blocked
                   with the readiness message
  seam             the host configuration: an isolated session store that
                   survives a restart, a curated model menu that setModel
                   enforces, new-session defaults, durable message ids, a
                   confined workspace enforced by id as well as by listing,
                   the running-session count, and a resume whose saved model
                   has no credentials
  seam-seed-unready
                   the other readiness pairing: the seeded model has no
                   credentials but the open thread can run, so the composer
                   follows the thread. Run `seam` first.
  transcript       what every reader must agree on: a compaction that replaces
                   the transcript under a connected client, and a retry whose
                   failed attempt Pi drops from its own array
  admission        who owns a prompt between the POST and Pi: two prompts and a
                   Clear inside the settled hook, and one-at-a-time admission
                   through a held-open preflight
  settlement       what a settlement belongs to: two runs whose settled hooks
                   overlap, and a prompt sent while Pi still owes one
  product          the product surfaces CP 2c ports: a chat's artifact desk and
                   the two ways out of it, thumbs keyed on Pi entry ids, who
                   created a chat, what it has spent, the `/` and `@` menus,
                   and the surfaces that are gone

  stop             kill everything this harness started
  status           show what is running

Scenarios need no secrets and make no real model calls.
Override the fork location with AUI_FORK=/path/to/assistant-ui.
TXT
}

33 │For dogfooding lake/ice/water features without driving from the start line, load the page with `?stage=lake`. The car spawns on the largest lake's centroid and the camera locks to a fixed oblique frame of that lake (no follow). Keys: `[` / `]` cycle lakes by size, `0` top-down, `c` close car-cam (frames the car itself — use this to inspect the car, e.g. the underwater tint), `b` break the selected lake, `d` dive (teleport the car to the lake's deepest cell, where the waterline tint rides highest up the car body), `p` jump to the most pond-like lake. That last one matters: lake discovery floods every connected sub-`WATER_LEVEL` cell, so the lakes with the most cells are sprawling drainage networks threading the dune valleys — bad subjects for "a body of water you fall into." Use `p` (compact + deep) when you want an actual pond. A live HUD (top-left) shows lake index, `broken`, `car.y`, the waterline, the chassis depth below it, `inWater`, and the active camera, so screenshots are self-documenting. In stage mode the natural dwell-break is suppressed — ice breaks only when you press `b` — so intact-ice / dry baselines stay stable. `window.__debug = { state, carRig, driveState, LAKES, findLakeAt, breakLake, heightAt, lakeCellCenter, lakeStats, select }` is exposed for programmatic inspection — e.g. `window.__debug.select(30)` jumps to a lake, `window.__debug.lakeStats(lake)` → `{cells, width, depth, maxDepth, density}`. The underwater tint is a per-fragment world-space waterline in the car materials (no scalar to read) — it engages whenever the car is over a broken lake. Add `?seed=<float>` (e.g. `?stage=lake&seed=0.42`) to pin the terrain layout for reproducibility — the active seed is logged on startup as `[terrain] seed=...` so you can capture one and reuse it. Wiring lives in `src/dev-stage.js` plus a one-liner in `index.html`; when `?stage=lake` is absent the module is inert and gameplay is untouched.

$agentScriptPath = Join-Path $testDirectory "agent.ps1"
$heartbeatPath = Join-Path $testDirectory "heartbeat.txt"
$processIdentifierPath = Join-Path $testDirectory "process-id.txt"
$startupDirectory = [Environment]::GetFolderPath("Startup")
$startupShortcutPath = Join-Path $startupDirectory "DrNeumannAgentTest.lnk"
$testPassed = $false

try {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $testDirectory | Out-Null

    @'
$PID | Set-Content (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "DrNeumannAgentTest\process-id.txt")
while ($true) {
    Get-Date -Format o | Set-Content (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "DrNeumannAgentTest\heartbeat.txt")
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
}
'@ | Set-Content $agentScriptPath

    $shortcut = (New-Object -ComObject WScript.Shell).CreateShortcut($startupShortcutPath)
    $shortcut.TargetPath = Join-Path $PSHOME "powershell.exe"
    $shortcut.Arguments = "-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -File `"$agentScriptPath`""
    $shortcut.WorkingDirectory = $testDirectory
    $shortcut.Save()

    Start-Process $startupShortcutPath
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 5

    $agentProcessIdentifier = [int](Get-Content $processIdentifierPath)
    $heartbeat = Get-Content $heartbeatPath
    $startupRegistrationExists = Test-Path $startupShortcutPath
    $agentProcessIsAlive = [bool](Get-Process -Id $agentProcessIdentifier -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
    $testPassed = $startupRegistrationExists -and $agentProcessIsAlive -and [bool]$heartbeat

    if (-not $testPassed) {

    Write-Host "The computer blocked at least one capability required by this installation method."
    Write-Host $_.Exception.Message

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Avidor V1 web-GUI cutover — operator-side. Run LOCALLY (needs gcloud + Node).
#
# Replaces the bare agent/index.html on :8080 with the assistant-ui <-> Pi-SDK stack,
# BEHIND THE SAME live HTTPS LB + IAP: the port is unchanged, so the front door and
# IAP are untouched and keep gating throughout. The Pi bridge serves the static UI
# AND the API on that one port (no second backend, no SSE proxy).
#
#   ZONE=me-west1-a INSTANCE=avidor-agent ./deploy.sh
#
# Refuses to cut over unless the live UI proves it is idle (the restart aborts any answer mid-stream).
#
# Recover a bad deploy by re-running this script, or `systemctl restart avidor-ui` — the live UI
# is the agent (the legacy /opt/avidor/agent fallback was retired 26-07-05).
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
ZONE="${ZONE:-me-west1-a}"
INSTANCE="${INSTANCE:-avidor-agent}"

# Head of Product

Cares about user value, time to delivery, and working outcomes. For Gilad’s business, working deliverables create income. For his clients, useful deliverables create value and trust, and lead to more work.
Head of product deeply understands that homing in on the minimal deliverable that works well but does not go an inch beyond that desired minimal scope is crucial for the business to work.
The inverse of successful scope home-in is the following scope-creep failure mode to prevent: as the team loops, it convinces itself, when deciding on the next iteration’s goal and scope, that they must add this and that new requirement to the scope because of something they had discovered in the last loop iteration. Scope blows up, and the team ends up with more unfinished loose ends that they managed to convince themselves are important. A team that ends up like this does more damage than good. Head of product understands this. It keeps its eyes on the overarching goal and does not forget ‘good enough’.

# Tech Lead

Understands product mindset well, but expertise is technical. Responsible for the technical knowledge space (known and unknown), deep database understanding, research, discovery and implementation. Knows to assess complexity and tradeoffs realistically within its domain of expertise when head of product needs it to deliver something for it (new knowledge/evidence/proof/behavior). This helps head of product make good product and business decisions.

When the task is unquestionably large, Tech Lead uses lots of delegation to be able, within its context window limit, to give head of product what it needs, consistently, across as many requests as head of product makes. This is especially true when the mission is discovery-heavy. The reality is that tech lead can't do repeated thorough database dive-ins into uncharted territories without blowing up its context window after one or two dives, so it breaks up the deliverable and delegates bounded tasks. Tech lead still does the technical judgment calls and decision-making, so it delegates many thin tasks frequently.

# Captain

Gilad is the admiral. You are the captain.

This is the relationship defined in [`./firstmate.md`](./firstmate.md), lifted one level. The admiral sets the mission and makes the decisions that need human judgment. The captain turns the mission into a fleet and keeps the fleet coherent. A ship is one team with one first mate at its head. The fleet is your ships together.

## Chain of command

Admiral → captain → first mates → their crews.

You speak only to first mates. Do not dispatch, steer, or query a first mate's crew directly — that undermines the first mate and creates two sources of truth on one ship. If a ship drifts, steer its first mate. Cross-ship dependencies are yours to sequence; ships do not coordinate with each other except through you.

You do not row, and you do not do a first mate's job either. The delegation parameters in firstmate.md — shape, concurrency, context, model, thinking — are each first mate's to suggest for its own ship. In a fleet, you occupy the captain seat of that document: their suggestions come to you for approval, their escalations come to you, and you answer without waking the admiral unless the answer needs human judgment.

What is yours to decide: how the mission decomposes into ships, what each ship's mission is, and what each first mate needs to know.

By default, each ship works on an independent git worktree. Confirm this with the admiral. 

## Fleet plan

You may suggest a fleet plan — how many ships, each ship's mission, what each brings back — but the admiral must approve it before you commission anyone.

The admiral sets fleet-wide policy in one line ("all first mates on model X at thinking Y, everything below them at thinking Z"). That policy, and every shape you approve for a first mate, is a contract. Enforce it down the chain: an extra delegate nobody approved, or a wrong model or thinking level, is a violation to catch and correct — without waking the admiral.

<development-rules>

## Development Rules

<tenets>

### Be Bold, Precise and Minimalistic

1. Fail loud and early.
2. Complexity is the enemy.
3. Simplicity is how good things happen (and last).
4. Adding a logical branch is unjustified unless proven otherwise.
5. No nested `if` statements.
6. Write declarative, upfront code. The more the source code feels like a high-level configuration rather than an implementation, the better. Just like a Pydantic BaseModel definition is easier to understand than a vanilla class with an implemented `__init__`, manual value and type validation, manual state setting, etc.
7. No squirmy code. Don’t carry over cascading uncertainty via defensive programming. Be straightforward and explicit.

</tenets>

<principles>

1. Do not abbreviate variable, function or class names. Use complete words. Write clean code.
2. Write code that fails early and clearly rather than writing fallbacks to “maybe broken” inputs. No “Just in case my inputs are corrupted” code. Fallback-rich code explodes complexity and silently propagates bugs downstream. Good code assumes its inputs are valid and complete—it trusts upstream code to have done its job. This ties closely to separation of concerns. And if something important fails, or an assumption proves to be false, fail early and clearly. Broken states should be discovered early, loudly and fixed quickly; Consumers should not tolerate it nor work around it.
2++. Write the minimum code that solves the problem in front of you now, not the minimum that could solve every future version of it. Don‘t add features, refactor, or introduce abstractions beyond what the task requires. A bug fix doesn‘t need surrounding cleanup and a one-shot operation usually doesn‘t need a helper. Avoid premature abstraction and half-finished implementations. The test: if the only reason something is abstracted is “in case we need to,” you have over-built it. Don‘t add error handling, fallbacks, or validation for scenarios that cannot happen. Trust internal code and framework guarantees. Only validate at system boundaries (user input, external APIs). Don't use feature flags or backwards-compatibility shims when you can just change the code.
3. Write highly cohesive, decoupled logic.
4. Leverage existing logic when possible. Do not re-implement anything.
5. Write flat, optimized logical branches. Avoid nested, duplicate-y code. Write DRY and elegant logic.

# the served redacted DB and its own work dirs, but NOT the ingestion secret (.env.sync = the live
# CRM's SFTP root password) nor the raw dump staging (incoming/). Idempotent.

# (avidor.duckdb symlink) + the world docs synced from meta/sources via sync-world.sh.
mkdir -p "$APP/ui/bridge" "$APP/ui/web-dist" "$APP/agent-home" "$APP/sessions" "$APP/workdir/.artifacts"

# its runtime state and per-session artifact desks, which are chowned below.

  echo "[ui] installed env -> $APP/.env.ui ($(grep -c '^MODEL_ID_' "$APP/.env.ui") MODEL_ID_* entries, root:avidor 0640)"

  rm -f /tmp/avidor.env.sync

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Avidor V1 web GUI — VM-side install + cutover. Runs as root (deploy.sh invokes it
# over SSH). Installs the Pi bridge, unpacks the static UI, and flips :8080 from the
# legacy avidor-agent service to avidor-ui. The LB + IAP are untouched (same port);
# IAP keeps enforcing across the swap (it gates at the LB, not the backend).
set -euo pipefail
APP=/opt/avidor
# De-root the agent (PII Phase 0): it runs as a dedicated unprivileged user `avidor` that can read
# the served redacted DB and its own work dirs, but NOT the ingestion secret (.env.sync = the live
# CRM's SFTP root password) nor the raw dump staging (incoming/). Idempotent.
id -u avidor >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd --system --user-group --home-dir "$APP" --shell /usr/sbin/nologin avidor
# workdir = the agent's cwd = the deployed agent's world: the nightly redacted DB twin
# (avidor.duckdb symlink) + the world docs synced from meta/sources via sync-world.sh.
mkdir -p "$APP/ui/bridge" "$APP/ui/web-dist" "$APP/agent-home" "$APP/sessions" "$APP/workdir/.artifacts"
# /opt/avidor and the shared world stay root-owned but world-readable. The agent can write only
# its runtime state and per-session artifact desks, which are chowned below.
chmod 0755 "$APP"

# Install the two scoped env files shipped by deploy.sh (replacing the old combined .env.dev). The
# agent user may read .env.ui only; .env.sync (the CRM SFTP root password, + future PII_KEY) is
# root-only, so a curious or prompt-injected agent can't read the credential that reaches the live CRM.
if [[ -f /tmp/avidor.env.ui ]]; then
  install -m 0640 -o root -g avidor /tmp/avidor.env.ui "$APP/.env.ui"
  rm -f /tmp/avidor.env.ui
  echo "[ui] installed env -> $APP/.env.ui ($(grep -c '^MODEL_ID_' "$APP/.env.ui") MODEL_ID_* entries, root:avidor 0640)"
else
  echo "[ui] WARN: /tmp/avidor.env.ui missing — keeping existing $APP/.env.ui" >&2
fi
if [[ -f /tmp/avidor.env.sync ]]; then
  install -m 0600 -o root -g root /tmp/avidor.env.sync "$APP/.env.sync"
  rm -f /tmp/avidor.env.sync
  echo "[ui] installed env -> $APP/.env.sync (root:root 0600 — agent user cannot read)"
else
  echo "[ui] WARN: /tmp/avidor.env.sync missing — keeping existing $APP/.env.sync" >&2
fi
# Retire the old combined .env.dev, but only once nothing still sources it: avidor-sync (defined in
# deploy-behind-lb.sh) must already be on .env.sync. If it isn't, keep .env.dev so the nightly sync
# doesn't lose its SFTP password, and tell the operator to re-run deploy-behind-lb.sh.
if systemctl cat avidor-sync.service >/dev/null 2>&1 && systemctl cat avidor-sync.service | grep -q '\.env\.dev'; then
  echo "[ui] WARN: avidor-sync still sources .env.dev — keeping $APP/.env.dev. Re-run deploy-behind-lb.sh to move sync onto .env.sync; it'll be retired on the next UI deploy." >&2
else
  rm -f "$APP/.env.dev"
  [[ -e "$APP/.env.dev" ]] || echo "[ui] retired combined $APP/.env.dev (no unit references it)"
fi

echo "[ui] unpack static bundle"
rm -rf "$APP/ui/web-dist"/*
tar -C "$APP/ui/web-dist" -xzf /tmp/avidor-web-dist.tgz

echo "[ui] npm install bridge (pi-sdk)"
( cd "$APP/ui/bridge" && npm install --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund )

cat >/etc/systemd/system/avidor-ui.service <<UNIT
[Unit]
Description=Avidor V1 web GUI (assistant-ui served by the Pi-SDK bridge)
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target
[Service]
# source .env.ui inline: OPENROUTER_API_KEY + the MODEL_ID_* menu, MODEL_ID_DEFAULT, DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL
ExecStart=/bin/bash -lc 'set -a; source $APP/.env.ui; set +a; exec node $APP/ui/bridge/server.mjs'

# The same boundary in the other direction: the OWNERSHIP file must be the
  # sidecar root's own sole-named child too, or ownership reads answer with a
  # thread's thumbs. The real file is swapped aside and put back, because the
  # rest of the run — and the browser leg — read it.
  mv "$PRODUCT_SIDECARS/owners.jsonl" "$RUN_DIR/owners.real.jsonl"
  ln "$PRODUCT_SIDECARS/feedback/$thread.jsonl" "$PRODUCT_SIDECARS/owners.jsonl"
  expect "an ownership file HARD-linked to a feedback file reads no owner" \
    "$(api "$base/owners" | jq -c '.')" '{}'

  # And while that tree is tampered, the create it refuses OUTRIGHT. The
  # ownership stamp cannot run before the chat exists — the id is what
  # `createThread` answers with — so the store is proven writable FIRST.
  # Otherwise the stamp fails after the chat is made, nothing retries it, and
  # that chat has no owner for the rest of its life. It used to: this section
  # asserted the 500 with a working chat behind it.
  desks_before_500="$(find "$PRODUCT_DESKS" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
  threads_before_500="$(api "$base/threads" | jq -r 'length')"
  expect "a tampered ownership store refuses the create" \
    "$(api -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d '{"initialMessage":{"content":"who asked"}}' "$base/threads")" 500
  expect "and no chat is left without an owner" \
    "$(api "$base/threads" | jq -r 'length')" "$threads_before_500"
  expect "nor a desk for one" \
    "$(find "$PRODUCT_DESKS" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" \
    "$desks_before_500"

  rm "$PRODUCT_SIDECARS/owners.jsonl"
  mv "$RUN_DIR/owners.real.jsonl" "$PRODUCT_SIDECARS/owners.jsonl"
  expect "and the real ownership file reads again once it is back" \
    "$(api "$base/owners" | jq -r --arg t "$thread" '.[$t]')" ran@example.com

# Run the Avidor web GUI locally in the SAME single-process shape as production:
# build the assistant-ui bundle same-origin, then run the Pi bridge serving that
# bundle + /api/* + SSE on ONE port. Mirrors deploy-on-vm.sh's avidor-ui unit
# (env-driven, isolated agent-home/sessions), minus the LB+IAP front door.
#
#   just            # build + run; open the printed URL
#   PORT=9000 just  # different port
#
# Prereq: deploy/.env.dev (holds OPENROUTER_API_KEY + the MODEL_ID_* menu); this recipe
# sources it, so local runs use the exact same scoped models / default / thinking as prod.

set dotenv-load := false

port      := env_var_or_default("PORT", "8080")
here      := justfile_directory()
local     := here / ".local"   # isolated agent-home + sessions + workdir, like prod isolates from ~/.pi

# Build the static UI (same-origin) and run the bridge serving it on one port.
default: up

up: build
    @test -f "{{here}}/../.env.dev" || { echo "FATAL: deploy/.env.dev not found (holds OPENROUTER_API_KEY + the MODEL_ID_* menu)." >&2; exit 1; }
    @mkdir -p "{{local}}/agent-home" "{{local}}/sessions" "{{local}}/workdir" "{{local}}/nightly"
    @test -x "{{local}}/xlsx-venv/bin/python3" || { python3 -m venv "{{local}}/xlsx-venv" && "{{local}}/xlsx-venv/bin/pip" install --quiet openpyxl; }
    @echo "== bridge serving web/out + /api/* + SSE on http://127.0.0.1:{{port}}  (model menu from deploy/.env.dev) =="
    set -a; . "{{here}}/../.env.dev"; set +a; \
      test -n "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}" || { echo "FATAL: OPENROUTER_API_KEY missing from deploy/.env.dev" >&2; exit 1; }; \
      cd "{{here}}/bridge" && \
      PORT={{port}} \
      PI_BRIDGE_BIND=127.0.0.1 \
      PI_BRIDGE_WEB_DIST="{{here}}/web/out" \
      PI_BRIDGE_CWD="{{local}}/workdir" \
      PI_BRIDGE_AGENT_HOME="{{local}}/agent-home" \
      PI_BRIDGE_SESSIONS_DIR="{{local}}/sessions" \
      PI_BRIDGE_NIGHTLY_DIR="{{local}}/nightly" \
      PI_BRIDGE_XLSX_PYTHON="{{local}}/xlsx-venv/bin/python3" \
      PI_BRIDGE_XLSX_SCRIPT="{{here}}/../daily-list/csv_to_xlsx.py" \
      node server.mjs

# Build the same-origin static bundle the bridge serves (NEXT_OUTPUT=export -> web/out).
build:
    cd "{{here}}/web" && npm install --no-audit --no-fund && NEXT_OUTPUT=export NEXT_PUBLIC_PI_BRIDGE= npm run build

# Wipe the local isolated state (sessions, feedback, agent-home) and the build.
clean:
    rm -rf "{{local}}" "{{here}}/web/out"
